key_concepts: Materials have chemical properties such as flammability, corrosiveness, and biodegradabili
Flammable materials like paint cans can catch fire easily if not stored properly.
Biodegradable materials like newspapers break down naturally.
Some materials rust easily when exposed to certain conditions.
Temperature is a measure of how hot or cold a material is.
Heat is a form of energy that transfers from one material to another due to temperature di
Heating materials can cause chemical changes.
Burning wood or coal is an example of a chemical change.
Improper storage of combustible materials can cause fire hazards.
Hazardous materials include insecticides and rubbing alcohol.
Oil spills can release harmful vapors that cause nausea, headaches, and skin blisters.
Knowing chemical properties helps prevent hazards at home and in school.
